From 46ef85f854dfa9d5226b3c1c46493d79556c9589 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Jack Wang <jinpu.wang@ionos.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 11:24:56 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] md/bitmap: fix GPF in write_page caused by resize race

A General Protection Fault occurs in write_page() during array resize:
RIP: 0010:write_page+0x22b/0x3c0 [md_mod]

This is a use-after-free race between bitmap_daemon_work() and
__bitmap_resize(). The daemon iterates over `bitmap->storage.filemap`
without locking, while the resize path frees that storage via
md_bitmap_file_unmap(). `quiesce()` does not stop the md thread,
allowing concurrent access to freed pages.

Fix by holding `mddev->bitmap_info.mutex` during the bitmap update.

Link: https://lore.kernel.org/linux-raid/20260120102456.25169-1-jinpu.wang@ionos.com
Closes: https://lore.kernel.org/linux-raid/CAMGffE=Mbfp=7xD_hYxXk1PAaCZNSEAVeQGKGy7YF9f2S4=NEA@mail.gmail.com/T/#u
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Fixes: d60b479d177a ("md/bitmap: add bitmap_resize function to allow bitmap resizing.")
Signed-off-by: Jack Wang <jinpu.wang@ionos.com>
Signed-off-by: Yu Kuai <yukuai@fnnas.com>

diff --git a/drivers/md/md-bitmap.c b/drivers/md/md-bitmap.c
index dbe4c4b9a1da..1d4a050dab3a 100644
--- a/drivers/md/md-bitmap.c
+++ b/drivers/md/md-bitmap.c
@@ -2453,6 +2453,7 @@ static int __bitmap_resize(struct bitmap *bitmap, sector_t blocks,
 		memcpy(page_address(store.sb_page),
 		       page_address(bitmap->storage.sb_page),
 		       sizeof(bitmap_super_t));
+	mutex_lock(&bitmap->mddev->bitmap_info.mutex);
 	spin_lock_irq(&bitmap->counts.lock);
 	md_bitmap_file_unmap(&bitmap->storage);
 	bitmap->storage = store;
@@ -2560,7 +2561,7 @@ static int __bitmap_resize(struct bitmap *bitmap, sector_t blocks,
 			set_page_attr(bitmap, i, BITMAP_PAGE_DIRTY);
 	}
 	spin_unlock_irq(&bitmap->counts.lock);
-
+	mutex_unlock(&bitmap->mddev->bitmap_info.mutex);
 	if (!init) {
 		__bitmap_unplug(bitmap);
 		bitmap->mddev->pers->quiesce(bitmap->mddev, 0);
-- 
2.34.1

The patch modifies `drivers/md/md-bitmap.c` to fix a use-after-free race condition between `bitmap_daemon_work()` and `__bitmap_resize()`.

**Modifications in `drivers/md/md-bitmap.c`:**
- Added `mutex_lock(&bitmap->mddev->bitmap_info.mutex)` before the critical section that replaces `bitmap->storage` (just after the `spin_lock_irq(&bitmap->counts.lock)` call).
- Added the corresponding `mutex_unlock(&bitmap->mddev->bitmap_info.mutex)` after the critical section ends (after `spin_unlock_irq(&bitmap->counts.lock)`).

**Relationship between modifications:**
The added mutex ensures mutual exclusion between the bitmap resize operation (`__bitmap_resize`) and the background daemon (`bitmap_daemon_work`). Previously, the daemon could iterate over `bitmap->storage.filemap` without synchronization while `__bitmap_resize` freed that storage via `md_bitmap_file_unmap()`, leading to a general protection fault. By holding `mddev->bitmap_info.mutex` during the storage update, the resize serializes with the daemon (which also acquires this mutex), preventing concurrent access to freed pages.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
In `bitmap_daemon_work()`: `for (i = 0; i < bitmap->storage.file_pages; i++) { /* access bitmap->storage.filemap[i] */ }`
In `__bitmap_resize()`: `md_bitmap_file_unmap(&bitmap->storage);`
Reason:
The daemon work iterates over `bitmap->storage.filemap` without holding any synchronization lock, while `__bitmap_resize()` frees that same storage via `md_bitmap_file_unmap()` after a non-blocking `quiesce()` call. This creates a use-after-free race where the daemon may access freed pages, causing a general protection fault in `write_page()`.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
`mutex_lock(&bitmap->mddev->bitmap_info.mutex);` (added before `spin_lock_irq(&bitmap->counts.lock);`)
`mutex_unlock(&bitmap->mddev->bitmap_info.mutex);` (added after `spin_unlock_irq(&bitmap->counts.lock);`)
Reason:
Holding `mddev->bitmap_info.mutex` during the critical section that swaps and unmaps the bitmap storage serializes the resize operation with the bitmap daemon work. Since the daemon work also acquires this mutex before accessing `bitmap->storage.filemap`, the race is eliminated: the daemon will wait until the resize finishes updating the storage pointer, preventing access to freed pages.
